title: Standardize deterministic benchmark environments and runner configs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our benchmark results (tokens/sec, p95 latency, and regression signal) are noisy across runs and CI images. Variability stems from mismatched GPU drivers, unpinned base images, and non-deterministic runner flags (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, NUM_WORKERS, ulimits). Purpose: define and enforce a single, deterministic benchmark environment specification (driver + CUDA + pinned image digests + runner config) and update CI/runners so daily and regression benchmarks are reproducible and comparable. This ticket scopes the spec, CI integration, and rollout plan for the serving/runtime benchmark fleet.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical 'benchmark environment spec' document exists with exact driver version(s), CUDA version(s), kernel parameters, and pinned docker image digests (sha256) for supported GPU types.

CI job 'bench-run:stable' uses the pinned images and runner config and produces run-to-run variance < 3% for stable long-sequence tokens/sec tests and p95 within expected noise band on baseline models.
Benchmark runner binary flags and env vars are versioned and stored alongside the spec (NUM_WORKERS, BATCHING_MODE, KV_CACHE_ENABLED, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, ulimit settings).
Regression detection pipelines (alerting) are updated to include an environment signature; alerts must only trigger for meaningful deltas after environment alignment.
Rollout plan to migrate existing benchmark runners to the new spec is documented and approvals from Infra and Serving Runtime are recorded.
proposal: Create a single YAML 'env-spec' artifact per GPU class (A100-80GB, A100-40GB, H100) that lists: driver package + version, CUDA toolkit minor version, kernel module flags, pinned container image sha256 for the runtime image, and required host config (ulimits, cgroups).
Publish pinned images in a canonical registry path: ghcr.redwood-inference/bench/runtime:<semver>-sha256-<digest> and ensure immutable tags for CI stable runs.
Add a small 'env-check' CLI used by CI and on-host runner bootstrap that verifies the host/driver/CUDA/image digest and fails the run with an actionable message if misaligned.
Lock benchmark runner defaults in the repo: NUM_WORKERS=2, BATCH_SIZE_POLICY=adaptive:latency(50ms), KV_CACHE=true, SEED=42 for stochastic layers where applicable.
Integrate environment signature (sha256 of env-spec + runner flags) into benchmark metrics output and regression checks so a comparison always includes environment parity.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): Draft env-specs for A100-40GB and A100-80GB; build and publish pinned images for these specs; add env-check to CI jobs but keep previous jobs as fallback.
Phase 2 (week 2): Switch nightly and PR bench jobs to 'bench-run:stable' with enforcement; run both old and new configs for a week and collect variance stats.
Phase 3 (week 3): Update fleet of self-hosted runners and Dedicated test pools to the pinned images and enforce env-check at bootstrap; monitor tokens/sec and p95 baselines closely.
Phase 4 (week 4): Flip regression detection to only compare runs with matching environment signatures and retire legacy images after a grace period.
testing_plan: Run the full benchmark suite (short/long sequences, chat streaming, multi-session KV cache) 30 times on both old and new envs to compute variance and p95 stability.
Synthetic noise tests: intentionally vary driver minor versions and confirm env-check detects mismatch and CI fails with clear remediation steps.
Verify regression-detection pipeline ignores runs without matching environment signature and only triggers when both model+env deltas exceed thresholds.
metrics_to_track: tokens_per_sec median and stddev across 30 runs
p95 latency for decode loop across workloads
regression alert rate pre/post environment standardization
CI flakiness (false positive alerts) drop percentage
time-to-detect real regressions after environment enforcement
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Pinned driver/CUDA combos may not be supported on all infra regions. Mitigation: maintain a small matrix of approved combos and clearly mark unsupported regions in env-spec.

Risk: Customer on Dedicated may run different drivers. Mitigation: regression pipeline will include environment signature and only compare like-for-like; document supported configurations for Dedicated customers.
Risk: Image pinning increases maintenance overhead. Mitigation: automate image builds with a scheduled job and a 'patch window' process for updates.
notes: Related artifacts: Confluence doc: /drive/benchmarks/env-spec-v1 (draft) and GH PR templates will be updated to require env-signature in PR descriptions.
Stakeholders: Serving Runtime (owner), Infra (driver/kernel), CI Team, Observability (regression alerts).
